records.source: וְיוֹסֵ֖ף הוּרַ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה וַיִּקְנֵ֡הוּ פּוֹטִיפַר֩ סְרִ֨יס פַּרְעֹ֜ה שַׂ֤ר הַטַּבָּחִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מִיַּד֙ הַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹרִדֻ֖הוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and bought him Potiphar, official of Pharaoh, commander of the bodyguards, a man, an Egyptian, from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
pieces: Meanwhile Joseph had been carried down to Egypt. The Ishmaelites who brought him there sold him to Potiphar, an Egyptian who served Pharaoh as a court officer and commanded his guard.

L.1: Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the guard, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.

R.1: The Ishmaelites brought Joseph to Egypt and sold him there. The buyer was Potiphar, an Egyptian. He was an officer of Pharaoh and head of the king's guard.

decisions.choice: Joseph had been brought down: the story returns to Joseph
decisions.reason: The sentence puts Joseph first and picks up where 37:36 left off, after the story of Judah in chapter 38. "Brought down" (hurad) echoes Jacob's words that he would "go down" to Sheol mourning his son (37:35).

decisions.choice: official ... commander of the guard: Potiphar's rank
decisions.reason: As in 37:36, saris here is a title for a royal officer, and the commander of the guard led the king's bodyguard. The narrator also stresses that he was "an Egyptian": Joseph now serves a foreign master in a foreign land.

decisions.choice: the Ishmaelites ... sold him to Potiphar
alternatives: Potiphar bought him from the Ishmaelites
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the sentence around to keep the long description of Potiphar at the end; the meaning is the same.

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְהִ֖י אִ֣ישׁ מַצְלִ֑יחַ וַיְהִ֕י בְּבֵ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו הַמִּצְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And was Yahweh with Joseph, and he was a man successful; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph, and he became a successful man while he served in the house of the Egyptian, his master.

L.2: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and made him successful. Joseph lived and worked in the home of the Egyptian who owned him.

decisions.choice: the LORD was with Joseph: the theme of the chapter
decisions.reason: The phrase frames the chapter: twice at the start (verses 2-3) and twice at the end in prison (verses 21, 23). The narrator uses the divine name here, though Joseph and the Egyptians speak only of "God". Whether in favor or in prison, Joseph is not alone.

decisions.choice: successful: things went well in his hands
decisions.reason: The word (matsliach) means one who prospers or succeeds; verse 3 says the LORD was the cause.

decisions.choice: and made him successful
alternatives: and he was a successful man
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two clauses as cause and result, as verse 3 does.

records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲדֹנָ֔יו כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא עֹשֶׂ֔ה יְהוָ֖ה מַצְלִ֥יחַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And saw his master that Yahweh [was] with him, and all that he [was] doing Yahweh [was] making successful in his hand.
pieces: His master noticed that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him, and that whatever Joseph undertook, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made it turn out well.

L.3: And his master saw that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with him, and [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all that he did succeed in his hand.

R.3: Potiphar could tell that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all of Joseph's work succeed.

decisions.choice: his master saw: even a foreigner could see it
decisions.reason: The Egyptian does not know the LORD, but he sees the results. God's blessing on Joseph is visible to outsiders, as it was to Laban with Jacob (30:27).

records.source: וַיִּמְצָ֨א יוֹסֵ֥ף חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינָ֖יו וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹת֑וֹ וַיַּפְקִדֵ֨הוּ֙ עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ וְכָל־יֶשׁ־ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And found Joseph favor in his eyes, and he served him; and he appointed him over his household, and all that there was to him he gave into his hand.
pieces: Joseph won his master's approval and waited on him personally. Then his master made him overseer of his household and handed over to him everything he possessed.

L.4: And Joseph found favor in his eyes and served him; and he appointed him over his house, and all that he had he gave into his hand.

R.4: Potiphar thought highly of Joseph and made him his own servant. Then he made Joseph the manager of his home and of all his property.

decisions.choice: served him: waited on him as a personal attendant
alternatives: worked for him as a slave
decisions.reason: The verb (sharet) is used of personal service to an important person, a higher place than general labor. Joseph is still a slave, but a trusted one.

decisions.choice: appointed him over his house: made him steward
decisions.reason: Great Egyptian households had a steward who managed the property, workers and supplies. Joseph will later have such a steward himself (43:16; 44:1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֡י מֵאָז֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֹת֜וֹ בְּבֵית֗וֹ וְעַל֙ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמִּצְרִ֖י בִּגְלַ֣ל יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְהִ֞י בִּרְכַּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ בַּבַּ֖יִת וּבַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was, from then he appointed him in his house and over all that there was to him, and blessed Yahweh the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph; and was the blessing of Yahweh on all that there was to him, in the house and in the field.
pieces: As soon as Joseph had charge of the house and of all the Egyptian owned, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed that household on Joseph's account. Whatever the man had, at home or in the fields, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s blessing rested on it.

L.5: And from the time that he appointed him over his house and over all that he had, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.

R.5: After that, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was good to Potiphar's household because of Joseph. Everything Potiphar owned was blessed, at home and out in the fields.

decisions.choice: blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake: the promise to Abraham at work
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham that others would be blessed through him and his family (12:2-3). Laban was blessed because of Jacob (30:27); now an Egyptian household is blessed because of Joseph.

decisions.choice: in the house and in the field: everything he owned
decisions.reason: The pair covers all his property, indoors and out: household goods, crops and herds.

records.source: וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֮ בְּיַד־יוֹסֵף֒ וְלֹא־יָדַ֤ע אִתּוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא אוֹכֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף יְפֵה־תֹ֖אַר וִיפֵ֥ה מַרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And he left all that [was] his in the hand of Joseph, and he did not know with him anything except the food which he [was] eating. And was Joseph handsome of form and handsome of appearance.
pieces: So the Egyptian left everything he owned in Joseph's hands. Having Joseph, he gave no thought to anything but the food he ate. Joseph had a fine figure and a handsome face.

L.6: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand, and with him [there] he did not know about anything except the food that he ate. And Joseph was handsome in form and handsome in appearance.

R.6: Potiphar trusted Joseph with all his things. As long as Joseph was there, the only thing Potiphar thought about was his own meals. Joseph was good-looking, with a strong body.

decisions.choice: he did not know anything except the food he ate: he left everything to Joseph
alternatives: he kept only his own food out of Joseph's care
decisions.reason: Most naturally the phrase means that the master no longer concerned himself with anything but his meals. Some read it as an exception: Egyptians would not eat with Hebrews (43:32), so the master's food stayed in Egyptian hands.

decisions.choice: handsome in form and appearance: like his mother
decisions.reason: The same words describe Rachel, Joseph's mother (29:17). The remark also prepares for what follows.

decisions.choice: the Egyptian / Potiphar
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַתִּשָּׂ֧א אֵֽשֶׁת־אֲדֹנָ֛יו אֶת־עֵינֶ֖יהָ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שִׁכְבָ֥ה עִמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And it was after these things, and lifted the wife of his master her eyes to Joseph and said, lie with me.
pieces: Some time later his master's wife set her eyes on Joseph. "Sleep with me," she said.

L.7: And it happened after these things that his master's wife lifted up her eyes to Joseph and said, "Lie with me."

R.7: Later on, Potiphar's wife began to look at Joseph with desire. She told him to sleep with her.

decisions.choice: lifted up her eyes to Joseph: looked at him with desire
decisions.reason: To lift one's eyes to someone can be simply to look; here it means to fix one's desire on him.

decisions.choice: lie with me: a two-word command
decisions.reason: In Hebrew her demand is only two words. Joseph's answer in verses 8-9 is long and careful.

records.source: וַיְמָאֵ֓ן׀וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֵ֣שֶׁת אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֵ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־יָדַ֥ע אִתִּ֖י מַה־בַּבָּ֑יִת וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יֶשׁ־ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he refused and said to the wife of his master, behold, my master does not know with me what [is] in the house, and all that there is to him he has given into my hand.
pieces: He refused. "You see," he said to his master's wife, "with me here, my master gives no thought to what goes on in the house. He has put everything he owns under my care.

L.8: But he refused and said to his master's wife, "Look, with me [here] my master does not know what [is] in the house, and all that he has he has put into my hand.

R.8: Joseph said no. He told her, "Because I am here, my master does not need to keep track of anything in his house. Everything he has, he has handed over to me.

decisions.choice: he refused: a firm and lasting refusal
decisions.reason: The verb (ma'en) is a strong word for refusing. Joseph's answer rests first on loyalty to his master and then on God (verse 9).

records.source: אֵינֶ֨נּוּ גָד֜וֹל בַּבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּה֮ מִמֶּנִּי֒ וְלֹֽא־חָשַׂ֤ךְ מִמֶּ֨נִּי֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־אוֹתָ֖ךְ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨יךְ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֜ה הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְחָטָ֖אתִי לֵֽאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: Not he [is] great in this house more than I, and not he has withheld from me anything except you, because you [are] his wife. And how will I do this great evil and sin against God?
pieces: He does not rank above me in this house. The only thing he has denied me is you, since you are his wife. How could I commit so great a wrong, and sin against God?"

L.9: He [is] not greater in this house than I, and he has not held back anything from me except you, because you [are] his wife. How then could I do this great evil and sin against God?"

R.9: In this house I have as much power as he does. The only thing he keeps back from me is you, because you are his wife. I could never do such an evil thing. It would be sinning against God."

decisions.choice: he is not greater than I: Potiphar has given Joseph equal authority
alternatives: no one is greater than I
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he is not great ... more than I" most naturally refers to the master himself: within the house, Joseph has as much authority as he does. Only his wife is excluded.

decisions.choice: sin against God: wrong against a person is also wrong against God
decisions.reason: Joseph sees adultery as betraying his master and, above all, as sin against God (compare 20:6; Psalm 51:4). Speaking to an Egyptian, he uses the general word for God (Elohim), not the divine name.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כְּדַבְּרָ֥הּ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף י֣וֹם׀י֑וֹם וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֥ע אֵלֶ֛יהָ לִשְׁכַּ֥ב אֶצְלָ֖הּ לִהְי֥וֹת עִמָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And it was, as she spoke to Joseph day [after] day, and not he listened to her, to lie beside her, to be with her.
pieces: She urged Joseph day after day, but he would not listen to her or agree to lie beside her or be in her company.

L.10: And it happened, though she spoke to Joseph day after day, that he did not listen to her, to lie beside her [or] to be with her.

R.10: She asked Joseph again and again, every single day. But he refused to sleep with her, and he even stayed away from her.

decisions.choice: to be with her: even to spend time with her
decisions.reason: After "to lie beside her", "to be with her" probably goes further: Joseph avoided her company altogether.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ כְּהַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א הַבַּ֖יְתָה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת מְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨ין אִ֜ישׁ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת שָׁ֖ם בַּבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And it was about this day, and he went into the house to do his work, and there was not any man of the men of the house there in the house,
pieces: But one day, as Joseph came into the house to see to his work, with none of the men of the household there inside,

L.11: And it happened on a certain day, when he went into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the household [were] there in the house,

R.11: On a certain day, Joseph came into the house to do his work. No other men from the household were there.

decisions.choice: about this day: on a certain day
decisions.reason: The phrase marks a particular day, one like the others until it was not.

records.source: וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂ֧הוּ בְּבִגְד֛וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר שִׁכְבָ֣ה עִמִּ֑י וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃
records.gloss: and she seized him by his garment, saying, lie with me. And he left his garment in her hand and fled and went outside.
pieces: she seized hold of his garment. "Sleep with me!" she said. But he ran from her and got outside, leaving the garment in her grip.

L.12: and she caught him by his garment, saying, "Lie with me." But he left his garment in her hand and fled and went outside.

R.12: Then Potiphar's wife caught hold of Joseph's robe. "Sleep with me!" she said. Joseph got away and ran outside, but she was left holding his robe.

decisions.choice: his garment: Joseph loses his clothing a second time
decisions.reason: His brothers stripped him of his robe and used it to deceive their father (37:23, 31-33). Now a garment is again taken from him and used as false evidence against him.

decisions.choice: he left ... and fled: he got away at any cost
decisions.reason: Joseph does not argue or struggle; he leaves the garment behind and runs. The word "garment" (beged) is the outer clothing.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ כִּרְאוֹתָ֔הּ כִּֽי־עָזַ֥ב בִּגְד֖וֹ בְּיָדָ֑הּ וַיָּ֖נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃
records.gloss: And it was, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,
pieces: When she saw that he had run outside and left his garment in her hand,

L.13: And it happened, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,

R.13: Now his robe was in her hand, and he had run off outside.

records.source: וַתִּקְרָ֞א לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵיתָ֗הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר רְא֗וּ הֵ֥בִיא לָ֛נוּ אִ֥ישׁ עִבְרִ֖י לְצַ֣חֶק בָּ֑נוּ בָּ֤א אֵלַי֙ לִשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמִּ֔י וָאֶקְרָ֖א בְּק֥וֹל גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: and she called to the men of her house and said to them, saying, see, he has brought to us a man, a Hebrew, to mock us; he came to me to lie with me, and I called out with a great voice.
pieces: she summoned the men of her household and said to them, "See here! He has brought in a Hebrew to toy with us. The man came in to me to lie with me, and I screamed at the top of my voice.

L.14: she called to the men of her household and spoke to them, saying, "See, he has brought us a Hebrew man to make sport of us. He came to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.

R.14: So she shouted for the men who worked in the house. "Come and see!" she told them. "My husband brought in this Hebrew, and now he treats us with no respect. He came to me wanting to sleep with me, but I yelled as loud as I could.

decisions.choice: he has brought us: she blames her husband
decisions.reason: She does not name her husband; "he" brought this man in. She turns the servants against the foreigner and against her husband's choice in one breath.

decisions.choice: a Hebrew: an outsider
decisions.reason: "Hebrew" is the name others use for Abraham's family (14:13). On her lips it stresses that Joseph is a foreigner, and the Egyptians kept apart from Hebrews (43:32).

decisions.choice: to make sport of us: to mock, with a sexual edge
decisions.reason: The verb (tsachaq) means to laugh, play or make fun of; in 26:8 it describes Isaac caressing Rebekah. She means that Joseph insulted the household by making advances.

decisions.choice: My husband
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear whom she means.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י כְשָׁמְע֔וֹ כִּֽי־הֲרִימֹ֥תִי קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ אֶצְלִ֔י וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃
records.gloss: And it was, when he heard that I raised my voice and called out, and he left his garment beside me and fled and went outside.
pieces: Hearing me raise my voice and shout, he left his garment beside me and fled outside."

L.15: And it happened, when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me and fled and went outside."

R.15: As soon as I started yelling, he ran out and left his robe behind with me."

decisions.choice: beside me: her story changes the facts
decisions.reason: The narrator said the garment was left "in her hand" (verses 12-13). She says it was left "beside me", as if he had undressed and run off when she screamed.

records.source: וַתַּנַּ֥ח בִּגְד֖וֹ אֶצְלָ֑הּ עַד־בּ֥וֹא אֲדֹנָ֖יו אֶל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And she placed his garment beside her until came his master to his house.
pieces: She put the garment down beside her and waited for Joseph's master to come home.

L.16: And she laid his garment beside her until his master came home.

R.16: She kept the robe close by her side. Then Potiphar came home.

records.source: וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּֽא־אֵלַ֞י הָעֶ֧בֶד הָֽעִבְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־הֵבֵ֥אתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְצַ֥חֶק בִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, came to me the slave, the Hebrew, whom you brought to us, to mock me.
pieces: Then she repeated it all to him: "The Hebrew slave whom you brought among us came in to me, to make a plaything of me.

L.17: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, "The Hebrew slave whom you brought to us came in to me to make sport of me.

R.17: She repeated to him what she had said before. "The Hebrew slave you brought home," she said, "came to me to take advantage of me.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew slave whom you brought: the blame laid on her husband
decisions.reason: To the servants she said "he has brought"; to her husband she says "you brought". She calls Joseph a slave and a Hebrew, both words that set him below her.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Joseph, who was sold and bought (37:28; 39:1); she uses the word to set him below her (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כַּהֲרִימִ֥י קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֥ב בִּגְד֛וֹ אֶצְלִ֖י וַיָּ֥נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃
records.gloss: And it was, as I raised my voice and called out, and he left his garment beside me and fled outside.
pieces: But as I raised my voice and cried out, he abandoned his garment beside me and fled outside."

L.18: And it happened, as I raised my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me and fled outside."

R.18: I yelled, and he ran out, leaving his robe here with me."

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹנָ֜יו אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּרָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה עָ֥שָׂהּלִ֖י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard his master the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, according to these things did to me your slave, and burned his anger.
pieces: Joseph's master listened to his wife telling him, "That is what your slave did to me," and he flew into a rage.

L.19: And it happened, when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, "Your slave did these things to me," that his anger burned.

R.19: Potiphar listened to his wife. "Your slave did this to me," she told him. Then Potiphar was filled with rage.

decisions.choice: his anger burned: against whom is not said
decisions.reason: The text does not say whom he was angry with. He puts Joseph in prison rather than having him killed, which some take as a sign that he did not fully believe his wife.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Joseph, who was sold and bought (37:28; 39:1); his wife's words repeat "the Hebrew slave" of verse 17.

records.source: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲדֹנֵ֨י יוֹסֵ֜ף אֹת֗וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֔הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אֲסִירֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲסוּרִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי־שָׁ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃
records.gloss: And took master of Joseph him and put him into the house of the prison, the place where the prisoners of the king [were] imprisoned; and he was there in the house of the prison.
pieces: He had Joseph taken and locked up in the prison house used for the king's prisoners, and there Joseph remained.

L.20: And Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison house, the place where the king's prisoners were confined; and he was there in the prison house.

R.20: He had Joseph thrown into the king's prison. Joseph stayed locked up there.

decisions.choice: the prison house: a fortress or round house
decisions.reason: The word sohar is found only in Genesis 39-40. It may mean a round building or tower; here it is a royal jail for the king's prisoners, attached to the house of the commander of the guard (40:3).

decisions.choice: the king's prisoners: two spellings in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text and the marginal reading of the Masoretes spell the word for "prisoners" slightly differently. Both mean the same.

decisions.choice: where the king's prisoners were confined: a jail for royal offenders
decisions.reason: This was a prison for people who had offended the king, like the cupbearer and baker in chapter 40. That Joseph is put here and not executed is unexpected for a slave accused of such an act.

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיֵּ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו חָ֑סֶד וַיִּתֵּ֣ן חִנּ֔וֹ בְּעֵינֵ֖י שַׂ֥ר בֵּית־הַסֹּֽהַר׃
records.gloss: And was Yahweh with Joseph and extended to him loyalty, and gave his favor in the eyes of the commander of the house of the prison.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph. He treated him with loyal kindness and won him the favor of the prison warden.

L.21: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and extended loyalty to him, and gave him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison house.

R.21: Even there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and was good to him. He made the head of the prison think well of Joseph.

decisions.choice: extended loyalty (hesed): faithful kindness
decisions.reason: Hesed is the loyal love that keeps faith with someone. Joseph is a slave in prison, but God has not let go of him.

decisions.choice: the chief of the prison house: the warden
decisions.reason: The title means the officer in charge of the prison, under the commander of the guard.

decisions.choice: loyalty
decisions.reason: Literal uses "loyalty" for hesed, as in 24:12; Balanced and Readable express the warmth of the word.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֞ן שַׂ֤ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֨הַר֙ בְּיַד־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣אֲסִירִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֹשִׂים֙ שָׁ֔ם ה֖וּא הָיָ֥ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And gave the commander of the house of the prison into the hand of Joseph all the prisoners who [were] in the house of the prison; and all that they were doing there, he was the doer.
pieces: The warden handed over to Joseph the care of every prisoner in the place, and Joseph directed all the work that was done there.

L.22: And the chief of the prison house put into Joseph's hand all the prisoners who [were] in the prison house; and whatever was done there, he was the one who did it.

R.22: The head of the prison gave Joseph the job of looking after all the prisoners. Whatever work was done there, Joseph was the one doing it.

decisions.choice: he was the one who did it: everything went through him
decisions.reason: The phrase means that Joseph ordered and oversaw whatever was done in the prison.

records.source: אֵ֣ין׀שַׂ֣ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֗הַר רֹאֶ֤ה אֶֽת־כָּל־מְא֨וּמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וַֽאֲשֶׁר־ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה מַצְלִֽיחַ׃ס
records.gloss: Not the commander of the house of the prison [was] seeing anything in his hand, because Yahweh [was] with him; and what he [was] doing Yahweh [was] making successful.
pieces: The warden never looked into anything entrusted to Joseph, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him, and whatever Joseph did, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made it succeed.

L.23: The chief of the prison house paid no attention to anything in his hand, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with him; and whatever he did, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made [it] succeed.

R.23: The head of the prison did not bother checking Joseph's work. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and made all of Joseph's tasks go well.

decisions.choice: the LORD was with him: the same pattern in prison as in Potiphar's house
decisions.reason: The end of the chapter repeats its beginning (verses 2-6). Whether a trusted steward or a prisoner, Joseph prospers because the LORD is with him.
